learning_outcomes.text: Learn scientific terminology of Materials science.

Improve academic skills pertaining to formality, caution, legitimate paraphrasing, writing citations and synthesising sources, critical writing, essay writing (with documented evidence), peer-feedback and academic presentations.
Notice formality and academic style conventions.
Notice scientific conventions in Materials Science Journals.
Transfer information from texts and visually enhance it in order to produce PowerPoint slides.
Write a laboratory report following a graph or chart.
Synthesise sources, summarise and paraphrase academic sources legitimately.

syllabus_topics: Formality and academic style conventions, citations and reference conventions.

Reading skills (skimming and scanning) on "Types of Materials", transferring information from text to slides, listening and note-taking skills, academic presentations using opening phrases and signposting language.

Collaborative skills using google docs about different types of Metals and their properties, reading an article on the FUTURE of metals, producing well-structured, coherent and cohesive paragraphs (identifying topic sentences, support sentences and concluding sentences).

Presenting and analysing statistical data, graphs and charts, writing reports using appropriate linking words and terminology (upward/downward trends, ratios, averages and numbers), producing a variety of visuals (mind-maps, diagrams, word tables or schemes).

Critical thinking skills by comparing different types of writing on "Bio-printing (2019)", noticing the structure, language and conventions of a scientific article about Graphene, a relevant blog post on Graphene and a school textbook entry.
How to give effective presentations, practicing peer-assessment skills using criteria for peer-evaluation and discussing strengths and weaknesses.

Classifying and identifying properties of solids, liquids and gases (using the English for Chemistry EAP textbook, Unit 1), legitimate paraphrasing strategies to produce a paragraph with citations and references.
Listening and reading various sources about Ceramics and advanced Ceramics, including all information elements, reminder phrases and references for Summary writing, language focus on Passive voice.

Introduction to essay writing (argumentative essay, counterarguments), distinguishing between descriptive, evaluative, cautious and biased language, reading and listening practice on Composites, practicing answering mock exam reading comprehension questions and tasks.

Polymers (from the book English for Chemistry EAP Unit 11), making a mind map connecting properties of Polymers such as thermosetting, thermoplastic, linear, branched, cross-linked, fibers, plastics and elastomers, solubility and rigidity, language focus on Gerund and infinitive, re-writing sentences avoiding wordiness.
Student Presentations (Slides in pptx or pdf format).
bibliography: Katsampoxaki-Hodgetts K. (2017) English for Chemistry EAP, Disigma Publications https://www.disigma.gr/english-for-chemistry-eap.html
